facts_of_case: Jose and Alice were married in a Roman Catholic Church. Jose suspected Alice's chastity after 2.5 months of marriage. He terminated her pregnancy and she was left at her parents' house. The marriage was declared null and void by ecclesiastical tribunals. Alice then filed for maintenance under Section 125(1) of the Cri. P.C.

legal_principles.principle: The High Court has jurisdiction to entertain a petition for nullity of marriage on the ground of force or fraud.
legal_principles.held: Thus the power to make decrees of nullity of marriage on the ground of duress or fraud was inherited by the Supreme Courts from the Ecclesiastical Courts and the High Courts inherited that power from the Supreme Courts.
cited_cases: B. Ignatius Anthoney Jayaraj v. Immy Margaret Florence, AIR 1978 Kant 69
T. Saroja David v. Christie Francis

legal_principles.principle: The ecclesiastical law under which a marriage was dissolved by the Church cannot affect or govern the Civil Law.
legal_principles.held: It was a case where the respondent wife had addressed a letter to His Holiness Pope Paul VI for grant of a dispensation dissolving the marriage between the petitioner and herself on the ground of non-consummation.
cited_cases: Re V. Alexander H. Mackonochie v. The Hon. Lord Panzance and John Martin (1880-1) 6 AC 424

outcome.final_order: The final court order quashed the decision of the Magistrate and Sessions Court directing Jose to pay maintenance to Alice.
